# Template: unit_circle
The unit circle: a radius to a point at the given angle, with its sine (dashed vertical drop) and cosine (horizontal drop) projections, a small arc marking the angle at the origin, and the point's exact (cos θ, sin θ) coordinates. Choose this scene for ANY request about the unit circle, sine, cosine, radians or degrees on a circle, or how an angle's coordinates relate to its sine and cosine. angle_deg is numeric and ANIMATES smoothly — tween it to sweep the point around the circle. While paused the viewer can drag the point round the circle (it settles on 30°, 45°, 60°, 90° … when close), and tap or scrub the angle to set it; everything follows. Its numbers read as {unit_circle.theta_deg}, {unit_circle.sin:2}, {unit_circle.cos:2}, {unit_circle.tan:2}, {unit_circle.quadrant}.
Parameter schema:
{
 "type": "object",
 "properties": {
  "angle_deg": {
   "type": "number",
   "description": "The angle in degrees, measured counterclockwise from the positive x-axis (default 45). Any real number — negative and > 360 both wrap correctly. Note: an animate that crosses a multiple of 360 (e.g. 350 -> 370) resets angle_arc/angle_label to their start rather than sweeping past a full turn — point/radius/sin_line/cos_line/coords_label stay continuous through that crossing regardless, so avoid animate targets straddling a 360 boundary if the arc mark itself must stay visually continuous."
  },
  "show": {
   "type": "array",
   "items": {
    "type": "string",
    "enum": [
     "sin",
     "cos",
     "tan",
     "coords",
     "arc"
    ]
   },
   "description": "Which parts to draw (default sin, cos, arc, coords). \"tan\" is accepted but currently has no dedicated geometry of its own."
  },
  "quadrant_labels": {
   "type": "boolean",
   "description": "Label the four quadrants I-IV (default false)."
  },
  "readout": {
   "type": "string",
   "enum": [
    "none",
    "deg",
    "rad",
    "both"
   ],
   "description": "Write the angle's size at the top left as angle_value: \"θ = 60°\" (deg), \"θ = π/3\" (rad — a multiple of 15° as a fraction of π, else decimals), or both. Default none. It follows every animate and drag, and past a full turn it keeps counting (390°)."
  }
 }
}
Element ids your commands can reference:
- circle: the unit circle (drawn at radius 240 for legibility)
- x_axis: the horizontal axis
- y_axis: the vertical axis
- radius: the line from the origin to the point
- point: the dot at (cos θ, sin θ) on the circle
- sin_line: the dashed vertical drop to the point, with its "sin θ" label, present when shown
- cos_line: the horizontal drop to the point, with its "cos θ" label, present when shown
- angle_arc: the small arc at the origin marking θ, present when shown
- angle_label: its "θ" label, present when shown
- coords_label: the point's "(cos θ, sin θ)" label with actual values, present when shown
- angle_value: the "θ = 60°" readout at the top left, present when readout is set
Examples:
Request: "Show the unit circle at a 30 degree angle, and animate it sweeping all the way around." → params: {"angle_deg":30}
Request: "What is 60 degrees in radians, on the unit circle?" → params: {"angle_deg":60,"readout":"both"}

Viewer can: Drag the point round the circle (it snaps to the 30 and 45 degree angles) or scrub the angle; sin, cos, the arc and the readout follow.

In YAML: `template: unit_circle` and `params:` per the schema above; commands name the element ids above.
